headline: Uruguay's Siege Undone by Saudi Arabia's Discipline
story: Uruguay imposed its will for ninety minutes, hoarding 63 per cent possession and forcing Saudi Arabia into a defensive crouch that never wavered. The Saudis offered almost nothing in possession—just 27 per cent—but their discipline was suffocating. With only 1.3 high-press phases to Uruguay's 6.4, they conceded the ball willingly, invited pressure onto their own half, and broke lines with the urgency of a side content to bury the draw.

Yet the numbers exposed both teams' wastefulness. Uruguay fired 27 shots, ten on target, yet mustered only 1.5 xG—suggesting hurried attempts from range rather than clear openings. Saudi Arabia's 3 on-target efforts from 7 shots hinted at clinical finishing when chances arose, but they created few. At 19.2 seconds to recover the ball, the Saudis were methodical; Uruguay pressed relentlessly at 12.9 seconds, yet neither translated dominance into goals. A draw that neither side will celebrate.

keyMoment.text: Both teams' wastefulness ensured neither would claim victory.

home.verdict: One goal on the break would have stolen the match from Uruguay's possession-heavy grip.
points: 44 forced turnovers created tempo; 19.2s recovery was methodical but left counterattacks unexploited.
Three on-target from seven attempts showed clinical finishing; press higher to reduce Uruguay's space.
1.3 high-press phases versus Uruguay's 6.4 ceded all midfield control; aggression wins group matches.

away.verdict: 27 shots for zero goals: possession without precision, dominance without reward.
points: 1.5 xG from 27 shots reveals hurried finishing; more patient build-up and precision required.
10 on-target efforts and 63% possession versus Saudi Arabia's compact 27% shows control without penetration.
6.4 high-press phases exhausted without payoff; midfield dominance never converted to clear-cut chances.

statLine: Uruguay's 27 shots from 63% possession generated only 1.5 xG: control became futility.
